description: Phase 2 Demo: RTGS Settlement Protocol. Generate a new standard-library module defining a stateful Settlement effect with Resource Hierarchy and verified atoms. The generated file MUST follow the Stateful Effects documentation pattern from std/effects.mm and the exact state-machine syntax: `effect Settlement`, `states: [Pending, Validated, Settled];`, `initial: Pending;`, and transitions `validate: Pending -> Validated`, `settle: Validated -> Settled`, `reject: Pending -> Pending`. Resource Hierarchy MUST declare `resource ledger priority: 1 mode: exclusive;` and `resource queue priority: 2 mode: exclusive;` with acquisition in priority order (ledger before queue) to prevent deadlocks. Each atom MUST declare `effects: [Settlement];` plus explicit `effect_pre` and `effect_post` contracts where applicable. Atom bodies MUST use `perform Settlement.validate;`, `perform Settlement.settle;`, and `perform Settlement.reject;` for primitive transitions. Cross-atom composition atoms (full_settlement, safe_settlement) MUST chain primitive atoms and inherit their effect contracts. Loop-based atoms (process_queue) MUST use `while` with `invariant:` and `decreases:` clauses for termination proof. Quantifier atoms (verify_all_balances_non_negative) MUST use `forall(i, 0, n, ...)` in `requires:` for universal properties. The key invariant is balance conservation: `(sender - amount) + (receiver + amount) == sender + receiver`.

atoms.name: submit_transaction
atoms.description: Submit a transaction for processing. This primitive operation keeps Settlement in Pending state (via reject transition, representing initial submission). Validates that sender and receiver are distinct non-negative identifiers and amount is positive.

atoms.name: validate_transaction
atoms.description: Validate a transaction by checking sender has sufficient balance. Transitions Settlement from Pending to Validated. Returns the remaining balance after deducting the transfer amount.

atoms.name: execute_settlement
atoms.description: Execute the settlement by finalizing the balance transfer. Transitions Settlement from Validated to Settled. The key invariant is balance conservation: (sender - amount) + (receiver + amount) == sender + receiver.
atoms.body_pattern: perform Settlement.settle; let new_sender = sender_balance - amount; let new_receiver = receiver_balance + amount; new_sender + new_receiver

atoms.name: full_settlement
atoms.description: Cross-atom composition of validate_transaction then execute_settlement with Resource Hierarchy. Acquires ledger (priority 1) before queue (priority 2) to prevent deadlocks. The sequence proves Pending -> Validated -> Settled with balance conservation.

atoms.name: process_queue
atoms.description: Batch processing of queued transactions with termination proof. Uses while loop with invariant and decreases clause to prove the loop terminates and maintains non-negative counters.
atoms.body_pattern: while loop with invariant: i >= 0 && i <= n && processed >= 0 && processed <= i && remaining >= 0; decreases: n - i

atoms.name: verify_all_balances_non_negative
atoms.description: Universal quantifier verification: all account balances in the array are non-negative. Uses forall(i, 0, n, arr[i] >= 0) in requires clause.

atoms.name: safe_settlement
atoms.description: Cross-atom composition of validate_transaction then execute_settlement without Resource Hierarchy. Simpler version of full_settlement that proves Pending -> Validated -> Settled with balance conservation.
